name: US500 CFD final-30-minute same-day continuation adaptation

source_references.citation: Baltussen, Da, Lammers and Martens (2021), Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum, Journal of Financial Economics
source_references.supports: Return through 30 minutes before the close predicts the final half-hour return across the paper's futures sample; headline trading results generally omit costs.

source_references.citation: Gao et al. (2018), Market Intraday Momentum, Journal of Financial Economics
source_references.supports: Related evidence that SPY's first-half-hour return predicts its final-half-hour return.

research.evidence_summary: Published evidence concerns futures and SPY. This draft freezes the locally available US500 CFD as a proxy and tests a stronger same-day return-through-T-minus-30 signal; transfer and net implementability are unverified.

feasibility.rationale: The fixed development segment does not establish the draft's five-year minimum, and next-bar-open entry, stopless/notional accounting, close execution, and verified early-close calendars are unsupported. Preserve as research evidence but do not adapt around these gaps.

market.session: US equity regular session 09:30 to 16:00 local time, or 09:30 to 13:00 on official early closes

data.frequency: Complete M1 bars with explicit half-open interval timestamps
data.minimum_history: At least five years spanning multiple volatility regimes; more is preferred
preprocessing: Map UTC bars to the official US regular session with DST
Set T from the official calendar including early closes
Require the prior official regular-session close, the bar ending at T-30, the next bar open, and the final bar ending at T
dependencies: Documented US500 feed and cost versions
limitations: US500 CFD is not the futures or SPY instrument in the papers
CFD session and close behavior may differ from the underlying auction
Candle data do not observe queue position or close price impact

hypothesis.behavior: The sign of the US500 regular-session return from the prior official close through the fully closed M1 bar ending thirty minutes before today's close predicts the sign of the final thirty-minute return.
hypothesis.mechanism: End-of-day hedging and leveraged-product rebalancing may create price-insensitive demand in the direction of the same-day move; this is a proposed explanation, not causal proof.
works_when: Closing hedging/rebalancing demand dominates liquidity provision
Two aggressive executions cost less than the conditional final-window return
fails_when: The CFD proxy does not track the relevant close mechanism
Liquidity providers reverse the same-day move
Spread and close slippage absorb the signal
falsifiable_predictions: Out-of-sample regression beta of final-window return on return-through-T-minus-30 is positive
The sign strategy has positive net mean daily return under documented costs
The final window outperforms predeclared adjacent-window placebos
A one-session-lagged signal has little predictive value

definitions.name: r_rod_t
definitions.timing: P[t,T-30] is the close of the last fully closed M1 interval ending exactly at T-30; P[t-1,T] is the prior session's last M1 close

definitions.name: direction_t
definitions.timing: Known only after the T-30 boundary bar closes

definitions.name: final_return_t
definitions.formula: P[t,T] / P[t,T-30,next_open] - 1 with sign applied for the short leg
definitions.timing: Entry uses the next M1 interval open and exit uses the final regular-session M1 close

entries.signal_time: Immediately after the M1 bar ending exactly at the official T-30 boundary has closed
entries.execution_details: Open of the next M1 interval, which begins at T-30; never the signal bar close
entries.order_type: Aggressive market order proxy at next M1 open plus spread, commission, and slippage
restrictions: No trade when r_rod_t equals zero
No trade for any missing/duplicate/out-of-order boundary bar

exits.time_exit: Close at the last M1 bar ending at official regular-session close T, with close-specific slippage stress
exits.end_of_session: Mandatory flat at official regular-session close, including early-close days
priority: Sample-end safety close if and only if the scheduled close is present

risk.position_sizing: One fixed normalized notional unit per session; report returns per unit and do not infer stop-defined R

experiment.baseline: US500 only, 30-minute window, next-M1-open entry, official-close exit, no filters, documented current costs
robustness_tests: By calendar year and volatility regime
Exclude largest one percent absolute returns
HAC and synchronized month-block bootstrap confidence intervals
costs: Charge half/full resolved spread as appropriate on both aggressive entry and exit
Stress close-specific slippage at 1.5x and 2x documented baseline
benchmarks: Always long for the identical final window
Random signs with identical trade dates and costs
experiment.multiple_testing: Primary asset and window are frozen. Log every asset, timing window, threshold, filter, and cost variant ever inspected; use family adjustment or synchronized max-stat bootstrap for placebo families.
rejection_criteria: Untouched test net mean daily return is nonpositive or its predeclared confidence interval includes zero
Result fails documented baseline costs or conservative close-slippage stress
Effect is concentrated in the largest one percent of days or a few crisis episodes
Final window is not superior to adjacent-window placebos
Unexplained failure of either long or short leg or boundary/calendar audit

pseudocode: For each official session, determine close T from the calendar
After the M1 bar ending T-30 closes, read prior official close and compute r_rod
If all boundary data are complete and r_rod is nonzero, enter its sign at the next M1 open with aggressive costs
Exit at the last regular-session M1 close with close-slippage costs
Record session, signal, entry, exit, both cost legs, and every placebo/control observation
required_libraries: V2 analytics/robustness tools where semantically applicable
edge_cases: Missing or duplicate boundary M1 bar
Spread spike at entry or close
implementation.computational_requirements: Low; one signal and trade per eligible day. Calendar and execution correctness dominate runtime.
known_backtester_gaps: The available fixed development segment does not establish the required five years of US500 history
Order.stop_loss is mandatory and outcomes are expressed in stop-defined R
Normal orders fill at current candle close rather than the next M1 open
No normalized-notional return path for stopless trades
Official early-close calendar support is not established for the US500 CFD proxy
